Q: How to use api to get and post data from different programmming languages? A:

Communicating between languages requires a protocol. If you are talking POST/GET in terms of HTTP then you simply need to build an endpoint to do what needs to be done. I.e in javascript you make an end point to accepts a post request that does something and returns something. Then in python you make something that sends this post request and does something with the returned data. Most languages share some common data structures that you can convert to and from i.e integers, floats, lists, sets, arrays etc. If you are talking more along a project that has multiple languages, perhaps a better question is whether you need these multiple languages.

Q: Is there a way to see the history of playwright tests that passed as well as failed in GitLab? A:

We ran into the same issue with Playwright and GitLab. GitLab’s UI is job‑focused and doesn’t keep good long‑term history per test, especially for passing tests, so simple questions like “has this test been flaky in the last few months?” meant opening lots of old pipelines and jobs by hand, which doesn’t scale on a big suite.

We worked around it by pushing the Playwright JSON results into TestDino as our external analytics system. There, every test (pass, fail, flaky, skipped) keeps long‑term history with duration, branch, environment, and commit info, plus simple flaky/failure rates. That cut 20–30 minutes of manual digging in GitLab down to a quick filter on a single test’s timeline and made it easier to see whether a failure was new or part of a longer flaky pattern.
